events.title: Anders Celsius is born
events.description: The Swedish astronomer and physicist was born in Uppsala. He later devised a temperature scale based on the freezing and boiling points of water, which became the Celsius scale.
events.significance: His scale is used for everyday temperatures and in science in most countries today.

events.title: First Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
events.description: Marching bands, floats and live animals from the Central Park Zoo made their way through the streets of New York City. Macy's staged the parade to celebrate the holiday and the start of the Christmas shopping season.
events.significance: The parade grew into a national Thanksgiving tradition watched by millions on television each year.

events.title: Jimi Hendrix is born
events.description: The future guitarist was born in Seattle, Washington. He went on to transform rock music with his inventive playing, use of feedback and studio experimentation.
events.significance: Many critics rank him among the greatest electric guitarists of all time, and his influence still runs through rock and beyond.

events.title: Harvey Milk and George Moscone are assassinated
events.description: San Francisco Mayor George Moscone and Supervisor Harvey Milk were shot and killed at City Hall by a former city supervisor. Milk had been the first openly gay person elected to public office in California.
events.significance: Milk became a lasting symbol of the struggle for LGBTQ+ civil rights, and the killings shook the city and the nation.

events.title: First partial face transplant
events.description: Surgeons in Amiens, France, reconstructed the face of Isabelle Dinoire, who had been badly injured in a dog attack. They used donor tissue to carry out the first successful partial face transplant.
events.significance: The operation opened a new frontier in reconstructive surgery and raised new questions about medical ethics and identity.
